source_text: ἀνοσίων αἱρετικῶν ἀφεγγῆ τε καὶ ἀμυδρὰ μυθάρια. Διηνεκὲς οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἀκατάληκτον τοῦ Σωτῆρος τὸ φῶς ὁρῷτο ἂν ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις, διερμηνευόντων ὀρθῶς τὰ θεῖά τε καὶ εὐαγγελικὰ κηρύγματα τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς διδασκάλων. Καθαρὸν δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον· τρυγὸς γὰρ ὥσπερ καὶ ῥύπου παντὸς ἀπήλλακται παντελῶς ὁ περί γε τῶν θείων δογμάτων ὀρθός τε καὶ ἀληθὴς καὶ ἀμιγὴς τοῦ χείρονος λόγος, ὃς ἀεὶ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐγείρει τὸν φωτισμὸν, οὐκ αὐτὸς οἴκοθέν τι προστιθεὶς εἰς λαμπρότητα τῷ Χριστῷ (κομιδῇ γὰρ εὔηθες τὸ ἀνθρώπου δεῖσθαι νομίζειν αὐτὸν), ἀλλ' ὅτι φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν καὶ ἀπαύγασμα τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑπάρχων ὁ Χριστὸς, τοῖς εἰς ὀρθότητα τῶν διδασκάλων λόγοις, τοῦθ' ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἀληθῶς, ταῖς τῶν πιστευόντων διανοίαις φαίνεται. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ διατί τὸ ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαιῶν εἶναί φησι; τοιγάρτοι λίαν ἀκριβὲς τοῦ λόγου, τάχα τι τῶν ἀναγκαίων ὠδίνει θεωρημάτων. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄριστα διανοῇ, καὶ τόγε εἰς νοῦν ἧκον ἐρῶ. Οὐκ ἐκ μόνων ἡμῖν ἐλαιῶν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τὴν τοῦ ἐλαίου χρείαν ἐπιτηδεύειν ἔθος τοῖς ταῦτα σοφοῖς, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἑτέρων ὅσων νόθων τε καὶ γεωδεστέρων σπερμάτων. Καὶ τὸ μὲν γνήσιον ἀληθῶς ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἔσται τῶν δοκιμωτάτων, κίβδηλον δέ πως τὸ ὡς ἐκ μοχλείας καὶ τέχνης, καὶ οἱονεί πως οὐκ ἀληθὲς, τὸ ἐκ σπερμάτων τῶν γεωδεστέρων, φημί. Οὐκοῦν λόγῳ τε τῷ ἀκιβδήλῳ καὶ ἀληθεῖ, καὶ διὰ σοφίας τῆς ἄνωθεν τοῖς ἀξίοις χορηγουμένῳ, τὸ ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἔλαιον εὖ μάλα παρεικαστέον. Τόγε μὴν ἐξ ἀνθρωπίνων ἐννοιῶν καὶ δαιμωνιώδους ἐμπνοίας ἐξευρημένον, τὸ ἐκ τῆς τινων τέχνης καὶ καπηλείας, καὶ νόθην ἔχον τὴν χρῆσιν. Ἀχρεῖος δὲ καὶ ἀπόβλητος ὁ τοιόσδε λόγος, καὶ ἀσυντελὴς παντελῶς πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἀπαράδεκτος ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις, οὔτε τὸ εὐῶδες ἔχων τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος («Οὐδεὶς γὰρ λέγει, Κύριος Ἰησοῦς, εἰ μὴ ἐν Πνεύματι ἁγίῳ»), οὔτε μὴν τὸ γνήσιον καὶ ἀθόλωτον τῆς ἀληθείας, καὶ εἰς χρησίμην τὴν ὄνησιν ἀναγκαῖον. Ἐπιτήρει δὲ ὅτι παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ προσκομίζεσθαι δεῖν τὸ ἐξ ἐλαιῶν ἔλαιον ὁ νόμος φησίν. Ὡς γὰρ ἔφην φθάσας, καρπὸς ἔσται παρ' ἡμῶν καὶ δωροφορία πνευματικὴ τῷ Θεῷ, λόγος ἀληθὴς, τὸν παρὰ Χριστοῦ φωτισμὸν οὐκ ἀφιεὶς ἀσθενεῖν ἐν τοῖς μυσταγωγουμένοις. Ἔξωθεν δὲ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, ἥ τε τῶν λύχνων θέσις, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἡ καῦσις. Φῶς γὰρ ὑπάρχων κατὰ φύσιν ὁ Χριστὸς, οὐ δεῖται φωτὸς, ἀλλ' ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἔξω θεότητος, καθὸ γενητοῖς, τὸ ἴδιον ἐνίησι φῶς. Ὡς ἐσωτέρω δὲ τοῦ καταπετάσματος ἡ κιβωτὸς ἦν, εἰς ὑποτύπωσιν καὶ εἰκόνα κειμένη Χριστοῦ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Εἶτά φησι· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν· Καὶ σὺ λάβε ἡδύσματα, ἄνθος σμύρνης ἐκλεκτῆς πεντακοσίους σίκλους, καὶ κινναμώμου εὐώδους τὸ ἥμισυ τούτου, διακοσίους πεντήκοντα, καὶ καλά
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] the aphengē (lightless) and amydra (dim) mytharia (little myths) of the anosioi hairetikoi. So diēnekes (continuous) and akatalēkton (unceasing) the Saviour's phōs would be seen in the Ekklēsiai, the didaskaloi in them diermēneuontōn orthōs (interpreting rightly) the divine and gospel kērygmata. Katharon the elaion: for of tryx (lees) and rhypos (dirt) apēllaktai (is freed) the orthos, alēthēs, amigēs (unmixed) tou cheironos logos about the theia dogmata, which always egeirei (rouses) the Saviour's phōtismos, not adding oikothen (from itself) anything eis lamprotēta to Christ (komidē euēthes to think he deisthai (needs) a man), but because being phōs to alēthinon and apaugasma of the Father, Christ by the logoi eis orthotēta of the teachers phainetai (appears) to the dianoiai of believers as what he truly is. PALL.: why ex elaiōn? lian akribes of the wording; perhaps ōdinei (is in labour with) some necessary theōrēma. CYR.: arista dianoē; I will say what comes eis noun. Not from olives only is it the ethos of those sophoi in this to epitēdeuein (produce) the use of oil, but from other notha (spurious) and geōdestera (earthier) spermata (seeds). The gnēsion truly from the dokimōtatoi olives; kibdēlon (counterfeit) that as from mochleia (forcing by lever) and technē, as it were ouk alēthes, that from earthier seeds. So to the logos akibdēlos and alēthēs, chorēgoumenos (supplied) through the sophia anōthen to the axioi, the oil from olives pareikasteon; but the [logos] exeurēmenon (devised) from anthrōpinai ennoiai and daimoniōdēs empnoia, [to] that from some people's technē and kapēleia (huckstering), nothēn echon tēn chrēsin. Achreios, apoblētos, asyntelēs (contributing nothing) pros phōtismon tēs gnōseōs tou Christou. So aparadektos (not accepted) in the churches, having neither the euōdes of the Holy Spirit ('no one says Kyrios Iēsous except en Pneumati hagiō') nor the gnēsion and atholōton (unclouded) of alētheia anankaion eis chrēsimēn onēsin. Epitērei: the nomos says the oil must be proskomizesthai (brought) from the sons of Israel; as I said phthasas (before), karpos from us and dōrophoria pneumatikē (spiritual offering) to God will be logos alēthēs, not aphieis (letting) the phōtismos from Christ asthenein in the mystagōgoumenoi. Outside the katapetasma the thesis and the kausis of the lamps. For being phōs kata physin Christ ou deitai phōtos, but to us tois exō theotētos, katho genētois (as originated), eniēsi (instils) his idion phōs. For esōterō (within) the veil was the kibōtos, keimenē eis hypotypōsin and eikona of Christ. PALL.: eu ephēs. CYR.: then: 'The Lord spoke to Moses: you take hēdysmata (spices): anthos smyrnēs eklektēs 500 sikloi, kinnamōmon euōdes half, 250, and kala[mou euōdous] [cont. §30].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [cont.] the ἀφεγγῆ (lightless) and ἀμυδρά (dim) μυθάρια (little myths) of the ἀνόσιοι αἱρετικοί. So διηνεκές (continuous) and ἀκατάληκτον (unceasing) the Saviour's φῶς would be seen in the Ἐκκλησίαι, the διδάσκαλοι in them διερμηνευόντων ὀρθῶς (interpreting rightly) the divine and gospel κηρύγματα. Καθαρόν the ἔλαιον: for of τρύξ (lees) and ῥύπος (dirt) ἀπήλλακται (is freed) the ὀρθός, ἀληθής, ἀμιγής (unmixed) τοῦ χείρονος λόγος about the θεῖα δόγματα, which always ἐγείρει (rouses) the Saviour's φωτισμός, not adding οἴκοθεν (from itself) anything εἰς λαμπρότητα to Christ (κομιδῇ εὔηθες to think he δεῖσθαι (needs) a man), but because being φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν and ἀπαύγασμα of the Father, Christ by the λόγοι εἰς ὀρθότητα of the teachers φαίνεται (appears) to the διάνοιαι of believers as what he truly is. PALL.: why ἐξ ἐλαιῶν? λίαν ἀκριβές of the wording; perhaps ὠδίνει (is in labour with) some necessary θεώρημα. CYR.: ἄριστα διανοῇ; I will say what comes εἰς νοῦν. Not from olives only is it the ἔθος of those σοφοί in this to ἐπιτηδεύειν (produce) the use of oil, but from other νόθα (spurious) and γεωδέστερα (earthier) σπέρματα (seeds). The γνήσιον truly from the δοκιμώτατοι olives; κίβδηλον (counterfeit) that as from μοχλεία (forcing by lever) and τέχνη, as it were οὐκ ἀληθές, that from earthier seeds. So to the λόγος ἀκίβδηλος and ἀληθής, χορηγούμενος (supplied) through the σοφία ἄνωθεν to the ἄξιοι, the oil from olives παρεικαστέον; but the [λόγος] ἐξευρημένον (devised) from ἀνθρώπιναι ἔννοιαι and δαιμονιώδης ἔμπνοια, [to] that from some people's τέχνη and καπηλεία (huckstering), νόθην ἔχον τὴν χρῆσιν. Ἀχρεῖος, ἀπόβλητος, ἀσυντελής (contributing nothing) πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ. So ἀπαράδεκτος (not accepted) in the churches, having neither the εὐῶδες of the Holy Spirit ('no one says Κύριος Ἰησοῦς except ἐν Πνεύματι ἁγίῳ') nor the γνήσιον and ἀθόλωτον (unclouded) of ἀλήθεια ἀναγκαῖον εἰς χρησίμην ὄνησιν. Ἐπιτήρει: the νόμος says the oil must be προσκομίζεσθαι (brought) from the sons of Israel; as I said φθάσας (before), καρπός from us and δωροφορία πνευματική (spiritual offering) to God will be λόγος ἀληθής, not ἀφιείς (letting) the φωτισμός from Christ ἀσθενεῖν in the μυσταγωγούμενοι. Outside the καταπέτασμα the θέσις and the καῦσις of the lamps. For being φῶς κατὰ φύσιν Christ οὐ δεῖται φωτός, but to us τοῖς ἔξω θεότητος, καθὸ γενητοῖς (as originated), ἐνίησι (instils) his ἴδιον φῶς. For ἐσωτέρω (within) the veil was the κιβωτός, κειμένη εἰς ὑποτύπωσιν and εἰκόνα of Christ. PALL.: εὖ ἔφης. CYR.: then: 'The Lord spoke to Moses: you take ἡδύσματα (spices): ἄνθος σμύρνης ἐκλεκτῆς 500 σίκλοι, κιννάμωμον εὐῶδες half, 250, and καλά[μου εὐώδους] [cont. §30].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …unholy heretics’ lightless and murky little fables. So the Savior’s light would be seen to be continual and unceasing in the churches, as long as the teachers in them rightly interpret the divine proclamations of the gospel. And the oil is pure; for the right and true teaching about the divine doctrines, unmixed with anything worse, is entirely free, as it were, of all dregs and dirt. It always stirs up the Savior’s light, not because it adds any brightness of its own to Christ (for it is utterly foolish to think that he needs a human being), but because Christ, being the true light (John 1:9) and the radiance of the Father (Hebrews 1:3), appears to the minds of believers as what he truly is through the sound words of the teachers.
Palladius: And why does he say the oil is to be from olives? Such exact wording is perhaps pregnant with some insight we need.

Cyril: You think very well, and I will tell you what comes to my mind. Those skilled in these matters, Palladius, are accustomed to make the oil we use not only from olives but also from various other seeds, spurious and earthier. The truly genuine oil will come from the finest olives; but the oil that comes, so to speak, from forcing and contrivance is somehow counterfeit and, as it were, not true, and by this I mean the oil from the earthier seeds. So we do well to compare the oil from olives with the word that is genuine and true, and that is supplied to the worthy through the wisdom from above (James 3:17). But the word devised from human notions and demonic inspiration is like the oil that comes from some people’s craft and peddling, and whose use is spurious. Such a word is useless and to be thrown away, and contributes nothing at all to the light of the knowledge of Christ (2 Corinthians 4:6). That is why it is not received in the churches. It does not have the fragrance of the Holy Spirit, for ‘no one says “Jesus is Lord” except in the Holy Spirit’ (1 Corinthians 12:3); nor does it have the genuineness and unclouded clearness of the truth, which is needed if it is to do real good. Notice, too, that the law says the oil from olives must be brought by the sons of Israel (Exodus 27:20–21). For, as I said before, a true word will be our fruit and our spiritual offering to God, a word that does not let the light from Christ grow weak in those being initiated into the mysteries. The lamps are placed outside the veil, and they are lit there too (Exodus 27:21). For Christ, being light by nature, needs no light; but into us, who are outside the Godhead inasmuch as we are created, he puts his own light. For the ark lay within the veil (Exodus 26:33), as a figure and image of Christ.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

Boundary: §29 opens mid-phrase ('ἀνοσίων αἱρετικῶν ἀφεγγῆ τε καὶ ἀμυδρὰ μυθάρια'), completing '...namely the' at the end of §28. 'φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν' echoes John 1:9 and 'ἀπαύγασμα' Hebrews 1:3; both cited as clear verbal allusions. 'πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως' is the wording of 2 Corinthians 4:6 (there 'of the glory of God in the face of Christ'); cited. 'σοφία ἄνωθεν' with 'δαιμονιώδης' and 'γεωδέστερα' echoes James 3:15–17 (wisdom 'from above' against wisdom 'earthly, unspiritual, demonic'); cited at 'wisdom from above' as James 3:17, with 3:15 behind 'demonic'. 1 Corinthians 12:3: Cyril has 'οὐδεὶς λέγει' (Paul: 'οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν'); rendered as Cyril words it. Uncited possible allusion: 'καπηλεία' (peddling) may recall 2 Corinthians 2:17 ('peddlers of the word of God'); not cited. 'τόγε μὴν ... ἐξευρημένον, τὸ ἐκ τῆς τινων τέχνης' has no main verb; the comparison is carried over from 'παρεικαστέον', rendered 'is like'. 'ὠδίνει' (is in labour with) kept as 'may be bringing to birth'. 'γενητοῖς' = beings that came into existence (creatures); rendered 'created'. The oil 'from the sons of Israel' points back to Exodus 27:20–21 quoted in §28. Ark within the veil: Exodus 26:33. The new quotation is Exodus 30:22–23 LXX; the section ends mid-word ('καλά|μου', calamus), so the English ends 'and of fragrant' and §30 continues 'calamus'. The citation for the rest of the quotation stands at its close in §30. Review: the oil 'from the sons of Israel' cites Exodus 27:20–21, since 'παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ' closes 27:21.

changes: 'divine preaching of the gospel' -> 'divine proclamations of the gospel' (two adjectives, plural)
Palladius' 'bringing to birth some needful insight' -> 'pregnant with some insight we need'
παρεικαστέον: 'may very fitly be compared' -> 'we do well to compare'
Nested parentheses around 1 Corinthians 12:3 removed; ἀθόλωτον restored as 'unclouded'
Exodus 27:20 -> Exodus 27:20–21; 'You also take' -> 'And you, take' (Καὶ σὺ λάβε)
Refs checked: John 1:9, Hebrews 1:3, James 3:17, 2 Corinthians 4:6, 1 Corinthians 12:3, Exodus 26:33, 30:22–23
